messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete Pokémon Eclipse: Aurelia Genesis as a playable browser RPG by connecting its existing maps, data, UI, and battle systems to story and progression.
- Preserve the existing game while adding Aurelia forms, starter evolution lines, regional legendaries, Soul Awakening, eight gyms, League, and postgame.

## Requirements
- Preserve party, inventory, player, captures, experience, evolution, and rewards.
- Improve the existing browser game rather than starting from scratch.

## Decisions
- Use `Battle.start(...)` for overworld battles and `js/main.js` for startup, persistence, controls, HUD, menus, and the game loop.
- Normalize inventory to `poke_ball`, migrating legacy `pokeball` saves.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented overworld and battle runtime in `js/world.js` and `js/battle.js`, with startup, persistence, and controls in `js/main.js`; updated `weighted(...)` in `js/core.js`.
- Added save/load support for `Game.storage`, migration from legacy `save.pc`, and storage reset for new games.
- Passed `git diff --check` and `node --check` for `js/main.js`, `js/battle.js`, `js/world.js`, and `js/core.js`.

### Active
- Wire trainer victories to badges and progression; add accessible interactions for story events, Soul Awakening, legendary encounters, League, and postgame.
- Place gym leaders and Elite Four trainers; fix Duneveil’s `leader_sahir` mismatch and gate League/postgame content.
- Browser-test full-party capture, save/reload persistence, and progression flow.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add persistent trainer-victory progression for badges, League, story, and postgame.
2. Complete gym leader and Elite Four placements; fix `leader_sahir` and gate League/postgame content.
3. Wire Soul Ember/awakening and static legendary encounters into world interactions.
4. Browser-test capture/save/reload and progression; rerun syntax and whitespace checks.

## Relevant Files
- `js/world.js`: Overworld interactions, trainer battles, encounters, warps, and healing; trainer wins currently only mark NPCs defeated.
- `js/maps.js`: Locations, NPCs, warps, Bramble Gym interior, League, and Soul Altar; progression events and destinations need connections or gates.
- `js/data.js`: Pokémon/forms, items, trainers, gyms, Elite Four, champion, postgame, static encounters, and `AWAKENINGS`.
- `js/battle.js`: Battle engine, rewards, capture, and `onEnd(result)`; trainer wins return `{ outcome: 'win', trainerId }`.
- `js/main.js`: Game state, startup, save/load, controls, menus, and persisted `Game.flags`/`Game.storage`.
- `js/core.js`: Shared utilities, including encounter weighting.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `js/core.js` is modified; `js/battle.js`, `js/main.js`, and `js/world.js` are untracked.
- Trainer victory results are available through the battle callback/promise, but no badge or progression flags are awarded.
- Gym leaders `leader_maris`, `leader_ignis`, `leader_sahara`, `leader_eira`, `leader_luma`, and `leader_draven` lack map NPC placements; Flora appears twice under distinct defeated-NPC IDs.
- Duneveil’s NPC uses nonexistent trainer ID `leader_sahir`; authored trainer ID is `leader_sahara`.
- Elite Four trainers have no map placements; League’s Lyra and Seraphine are ungated; `seraphine_eclipse` and rematch trainers are not placed.
- `AWAKENINGS` and `STATIC_ENCOUNTERS` are definitions without runtime interaction. The Origins altar has `interact: 'soul_ember'`, but `World.interact()` handles only healing and object text/default dialogue.
- Battle damage uses species abilities and moves, but `js/battle.js` has no Soul Awakening implementation.
- Capture logic sends catches to the party if it has fewer than six members and otherwise to `session.state.pc` or `session.state.storage`; browser verification of persistence remains pending.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e4257613affecSjKm2rQprq7bn" state="completed" description="Inspect progression and maps">
## Findings

- **Trainer victories have a usable hook, but victory metadata is not applied.** In [`/home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/world.js:79–85`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/world.js ), `World.interact()` starts a trainer battle and, on a win, records `state.defeated[npc.id] = true`. In [`/home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/battle.js:654–664`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/battle.js ), `finishVictory()` pays the trainer reward and displays its win text, then ends the battle. It does **not** award `trainer.badge` or trigger League, postgame, or story progression.
- **Progress can be persisted already.** [`/home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/main.js:31–49, 61–79, 91–96`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/main.js ) saves/restores `Game.flags` and defeated NPC IDs, and aliases `World.state.flags` to `Game.flags`. However, world persistence does not include `World.state.lastMap` (it is only set in [`world.js:36–40`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/world.js )). Don’t rely on `lastMap` for a persistent story checkpoint unless it is added to the save.
- **Trainer metadata already describes progression, but it is inert.** [`/home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/data.js:849–905, 1005–1016`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/data.js ) defines badge numbers, Elite Four/champion properties, postgame trainers, and a superboss. The victory path does not interpret those properties.
- **NPC and trainer IDs need to be reconciled.** Completion is keyed by NPC ID, not trainer ID: Flora appears as `leader_flora` outdoors and `flora_gym` indoors, both using trainer `leader_flora` ([`/home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/maps.js:128, 211`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/maps.js )). Those placements can therefore track as separate defeats. There are also metadata/placement mismatches: Duneveil places `leader_sahir` ([`maps.js:145`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/maps.js )), while the corresponding defined gym leaders include `leader_sahara` and `leader_maris` ([`data.js:854–864`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/data.js )). Review map trainer references against `TRAINERS` before wiring progression.
- **League progression and gates are not implemented.** The League map places Lyra and the Champion, but none of the Elite Four ([`/home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/maps.js:182–187`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/maps.js )); their trainer definitions are in `data.js:883–905`. League-to-Skyfall and other routes are ordinary links ([`maps.js:213–222`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/maps.js )). `transition()` simply calls `setMap()` ([`world.js:42–44`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/world.js )); neither it nor the movement/interaction path checks badge or story flags. Props such as the Obsidian Gate and Victory Arch are static blocked objects, not progression checks ([`maps.js:175, 184`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/maps.js )).
- **Story flags have storage but no general interaction mechanism.** The flags object is available and saved, but `World.interact()` only handles healing, object text, or generic ambience for objects ([`world.js:88–95`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/world.js )). It does not interpret an object’s `interact` action or conditional dialogue. The Origins altar declares `interact: 'soul_ember'` ([`maps.js:194–197`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/maps.js )), but that action currently has no handler.
- **Soul Ember and Awakening are mostly definitions, not a connected feature.** Soul Ember is a key item in [`/home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/data.js:808`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/data.js ). Awakening-related forms and unlock metadata are defined in `data.js:688–780`, but no altar interaction awards the item or connects it to an awakening action. Battle’s bag deliberately excludes key items and TMs ([`/home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/battle.js:496–507`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/battle.js )); don’t implement Awakening as an in-battle bag item without changing that design.
- **Static encounters are data-only in the searched files.** [`/home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/data.js:1105–1110`]( /home/runner/work/Pokemon/Pokemon/js/data.js ) defines Zekrom, Reshiram, and Kyurem, but no map trigger or static-encounter battle path was found. `World.encounter()` uses the map’s grass encounter table (`world.js:108`), not `STATIC_ENCOUNTERS`.

## Minimal coherent changes

1. **Use one successful-trainer-victory progression handler.** Invoke it from the existing `World.interact()` battle `onEnd` callback, only when `r.outcome === 'win'`. Look up the trainer metadata and apply badge/story/postgame effects there; keep `finishVictory()` focused on battle rewards and win text. Persist the resulting flags with the existing save path.
2. **Choose a consistent completion key.** If defeating a trainer should count everywhere that trainer appears, key completion by trainer ID rather than placement NPC ID. Reconcile map references with `TRAINERS` and add or place the intended gym leaders and Elite Four. Give rematches distinct trainer IDs if they must remain independently repeatable.
3. **Put progression checks on actual transitions.** Add a shared gate check to gameplay warp/transition handling (the central `transition()` path covers both stepping onto a warp and interacting with one), with explicit requirements for League, postgame, and story gates. Keep decorative blocked props separate from the authorization logic.
4. **Give objects and story NPCs explicit actions.** Extend object/NPC interaction handling to recognize action IDs and conditional dialogue, then update flags/inventory through those actions. For Soul Ember, the altar should check prerequisites, award the key item or persistent unlock flag, and invoke the Awakening flow; the flag/item should be saved.
5. **Add a static-encounter trigger and persistent outcome.** Associate an encounter ID with a map object/NPC and dispatch it to a dedicated battle start using the static definition. Record the resolved/captured state in saved flags so the encounter’s repeat behavior is explicit.

These are file-navigation findings only; no files were changed.
</subagent>

## Objective
- Complete Pokémon Eclipse: Aurelia Genesis as a playable browser RPG by connecting its existing maps, data, UI, and battle systems to story and progression.
- Preserve the existing game while adding Aurelia forms, starter evolution lines, regional legendaries, Soul Awakening, eight gyms, League, and postgame.

## Requirements
- Preserve party, inventory, player, captures, experience, evolution, and rewards.
- Improve the existing browser game rather than starting from scratch.

## Decisions
- Use `Battle.start(...)` for overworld battles and `js/main.js` for startup, persistence, controls, HUD, menus, and the game loop.
- Normalize inventory to `poke_ball`, migrating legacy `pokeball` saves.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented overworld and battle runtime in `js/world.js` and `js/battle.js`, with startup, persistence, and controls in `js/main.js`; updated `weighted(...)` in `js/core.js`.
- Added save/load support for `Game.storage`, migration from legacy `save.pc`, and storage reset for new games.
- Passed `git diff --check` and `node --check` for `js/main.js`, `js/battle.js`, `js/world.js`, and `js/core.js`.

### Active
- Add persistent trainer-victory progression for badges, League, story, and postgame.
- Place remaining gym leaders and Elite Four; correct Duneveil’s `leader_sahir` reference to `leader_sahara`; gate League and postgame content.
- Wire Soul Ember, Soul Awakening, and static legendary encounters into world interactions and battles.
- Browser-test full-party capture, save/reload persistence, and progression flow.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add persistent trainer-victory progression for badges, League, story, and postgame.
2. Place remaining gym leaders and Elite Four; correct `leader_sahir` and gate League/postgame content.
3. Wire Soul Ember, Soul Awakening, and static legendary encounters to world interactions and battle behavior.
4. Browser-test capture/save/reload and progression; rerun syntax and whitespace checks.

## Relevant Files
- `js/world.js`: Overworld interactions, trainer battles, encounters, warps, and healing.
- `js/maps.js`: Locations, NPCs, warps, Bramble Gym interior, League, and Soul Altar.
- `js/data.js`: Pokémon/forms, items, trainers, gyms, Elite Four, champion, postgame, static encounters, and `AWAKENINGS`.
- `js/battle.js`: Battle engine, rewards, capture, and `onEnd(result)`.
- `js/main.js`: Game state, startup, save/load, controls, menus, and persisted `Game.flags`/`Game.storage`.
- `js/core.js`: Shared utilities, including encounter weighting.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `js/core.js` is modified; `js/battle.js`, `js/main.js`, and `js/world.js` are untracked.
- Trainer victory results are available through the battle callback/promise, but `js/world.js` currently only marks the NPC defeated; progression flags and badges are not awarded there.
- Gym leaders `leader_maris`, `leader_ignis`, `leader_sahara`, `leader_eira`, `leader_luma`, and `leader_draven` lack map NPC placements; Flora appears twice under distinct defeated-NPC IDs.
- Duneveil’s NPC points to nonexistent trainer `leader_sahir`; the authored trainer is `leader_sahara`.
- Elite Four trainers have no map placements; League’s `ace_lyra` and `champion_seraphine` are ungated; `seraphine_eclipse` and rematch trainers are not placed.
- `AWAKENINGS` and `STATIC_ENCOUNTERS` are definitions without runtime interaction. The Origins altar has `interact: 'soul_ember'`, but `World.interact()` handles only healing and object text/default dialogue.
- Battle combat uses species abilities and moves, but `js/battle.js` has no Soul Awakening implementation.
- Capture sends Pokémon to the party if it has fewer than six members and otherwise to `session.state.pc` or `session.state.storage`; browser verification of persistence remains pending.
